mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best describes parallel lines?

options.A: Lines that intersect at a right angle.
options.B: Lines that lie in the same plane and never meet, no matter how far they are extended.
options.C: Lines that cross each other at any point.
options.D: Lines that are curved in the same direction.

mcqs.answer: Lines that lie in the same plane and never meet, no matter how far they are extended.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are defined as lines that are in the same plane and do not intersect, regardless of how far they are extended. Option B states this definition correctly. Option A describes perpendicular lines, Option C describes intersecting lines, and Option D describes a property of curves, not straight lines.

mcqs.question: A railway track consists of two long metal rails that run side by side. Which pair of lines below correctly represents these rails?

options.A: Two lines that cross each other at a point.
options.B: Two lines that are at right angles to each other.
options.C: Two lines that are in the same plane and never meet, even when extended.
options.D: Two lines that curve away from each other.

mcqs.answer: Two lines that are in the same plane and never meet, even when extended.
mcqs.explanation: Railway rails are designed to stay the same distance apart and never intersect, which matches the definition of parallel lines (Option C). Options A and B describe intersecting and perpendicular lines, while Option D describes diverging lines, none of which apply to railway rails.

mcqs.question: In the figure below, three straight lines are drawn. Line AB is horizontal, line CD slopes upward to the right, and line EF is also horizontal. Which pair of lines are parallel?
mcqs.explanation: Lines AB and EF are both horizontal, meaning they lie in the same plane and never meet; therefore they are parallel. Line CD has a different slope, so it is not parallel to the horizontal lines. Option D is incorrect because CD is not parallel to the others.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Why are the opposite sides of a rectangular door frame considered parallel?

options.A: Because they intersect at the corners.
options.B: Because they are equal in length.
options.C: Because they lie in the same plane and never meet, even if extended.

mcqs.answer: Because they lie in the same plane and never meet, even if extended.
mcqs.explanation: Opposite sides of a rectangle are straight, lie in the same plane, and never intersect, which matches the definition of parallel lines. Equality of length (Option B) is a property of rectangles but does not define parallelism. Options A and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares parallel lines with intersecting lines?

options.A: Parallel lines meet at a right angle, while intersecting lines never meet.
options.B: Parallel lines are always curved, whereas intersecting lines are straight.
options.C: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never intersect; intersecting lines cross each other at some point.
options.D: Parallel lines can be in different planes, while intersecting lines must be in the same plane.

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never intersect; intersecting lines cross each other at some point.
mcqs.explanation: Option C accurately describes the distinction: parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, while intersecting lines cross at a point. Options A, B, and D contain incorrect statements about angles, curvature, and planes.

mcqs.question: If line l is parallel to line m and line m is parallel to line n, which of the following must be true?

options.A: Line l is perpendicular to line n.
options.C: Line l is parallel to line n.
options.D: Line l and line n are the same line.

mcqs.answer: Line l is parallel to line n.
mcqs.explanation: Parallelism is a transitive relation: if l ∥ m and m ∥ n, then l ∥ n. Therefore, Option C is correct. Options A and B contradict the definition of parallel lines, and Option D is not required; distinct parallel lines can be separate.

mcqs.question: In a simple drawing, two straight lines are drawn side by side and never meet, even when extended. What are these lines called?
mcqs.explanation: Lines that are in the same plane and never intersect, no matter how far they are extended, are defined as parallel lines. Hence Option C is correct. The other options describe different relationships.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday objects shows parallel lines?

options.A: The edges of a book cover that are opposite each other
options.B: The two sides of a V-shaped road sign
options.C: The intersecting lines of a crosswalk
options.D: The diagonal lines on a checkerboard

mcqs.answer: The edges of a book cover that are opposite each other
mcqs.explanation: Opposite edges of a book cover are straight, lie in the same plane, and never meet, making them parallel. The V-shaped sign has sides that converge (not parallel), crosswalk lines intersect, and checkerboard diagonals cross each other.
